_note: Week of August 10–16, 2026. Built around Jake's inflammation and enlarged spleen — leaning on general, doctor-safe anti-inflammatory eating principles (more fatty fish, colorful vegetables and fruit, whole grains, legumes, and healthy fats; less processed food, fried food, heavy cream/cheese, and added sugar). Turmeric and fresh ginger show up across a few dishes for their anti-inflammatory reputation. The frozen pork loin anchors Monday (lean-trimmed, roasted, not fried), with extra for Tuesday's Pita Tuesday. Wed and Fri stay fish nights, which fits nicely here. Sunday leans on avocado for healthy fat instead of a heavier cheese pour. Cheese generally stays light-handed this week rather than a headline ingredient. No raw onion, mushrooms, lentils, okra, or eggplant; Laine's lunch and Jake's reheat-friendly saucy lunch format stay as established.

tzatziki.name: Turmeric-Ginger Yogurt Sauce
tzatziki.note: This week's tzatziki-slot sauce, built around two of the more well-known anti-inflammatory spices. Nonfat Greek yogurt base, so it stays light rather than a heavy high-fat dairy sauce. Goes on Tuesday's pita as the main event; a spoonful also works over the salmon or the chickpea bowl if there's extra. Makes about 2 cups (9 servings of ¼ cup), keeps 4–5 days.
steps: Grate the fresh ginger and garlic directly into the yogurt — a microplane works well for both.
Stir in the turmeric, lemon juice, and olive oil until the color is even.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Chill at least 20 min before serving.
Keeps 4–5 days — the flavor mellows and rounds out by day 2.

dinners.name: Herb-Roasted Pork Loin with Sweet Potato & Broccoli
dinners.note: Uses the frozen pork loin — trimmed of visible fat and roasted, not fried or creamed, which is the main dietary lever for inflammation: lean preparation over rich or fried. Sweet potato instead of white for more fiber and beta-carotene. Cook extra pork alongside for Tuesday.

ingredients.item: Pork loin — Jake 260g, Laine 160g raw, trimmed (buy ~160g extra for Tuesday)
Sweet potato — Jake ~235g, Laine ~170g, cut into wedges
Olive oil — Jake 1 tbsp, Laine scant ¾ tbsp

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Trim any visible fat cap on the pork loin down to a thin layer.
Toss the sweet potato wedges with half the olive oil and spice mix, roast 15 min.
Rub the pork loin (both Monday's and Tuesday's extra piece, roasted together) with the remaining oil, garlic, and spice mix.
Add the pork to the pan with the potatoes, roast 20–25 min more until the pork hits 145°F internal. Rest 5 min before slicing. Steam the broccoli separately.
Set the extra plain pork aside once cooled for Tuesday. Jake gets the bigger portion.

dinners.name: Pork & Shrimp Pita Pockets with Turmeric-Ginger Yogurt Sauce
dinners.note: Standing leftovers-plus-a-treat night. Monday's reserved pork warmed through with a shrimp treat, pita, and a generous spoonful of this week's sauce.

ingredients.item: Reserved pork loin from Monday — Jake 160g, Laine 100g, sliced
Frozen shrimp — Jake 120g, Laine 75g raw, peeled
Whole wheat pita — Jake 1⅓, Laine ⅘
Turmeric-Ginger Yogurt Sauce — Jake 1¼ servings, Laine scant 1 serving
Olive oil — Jake ½ tbsp, Laine scant ⅓ tbsp

steps: Warm the sliced pork through in a skillet with a little olive oil.
In the same pan, sear the shrimp with garlic and spice mix, 2–3 min per side until just pink.
Warm the pitas. Split and fill with pork, shrimp, romaine, and cherry tomato.
Finish with a generous spoonful of the turmeric-ginger sauce. Jake gets the bigger pita.

dinners.name: Ginger-Turmeric Baked Salmon, Quinoa & Broccoli
dinners.note: Fish night. Salmon already brings good omega-3s; ginger and turmeric layer on top of that.

ingredients.item: Olive oil — Jake scant 1 tbsp, Laine scant ½ tbsp
Ground turmeric — Jake ½ tsp, Laine ⅓ tsp
Lemon juice — Jake ½ tbsp, Laine scant ½ tbsp

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Cook the quinoa according to package directions.
Pat the salmon dry, place on a lined sheet pan. Mix grated ginger, turmeric, garlic, olive oil, and lemon juice into a paste, rub over the salmon.
Bake 12–15 min until it flakes easily. Steam the broccoli alongside.
Plate quinoa, salmon, and broccoli together. Jake gets the bigger fillet.

dinners.name: Turmeric-Lemon Chicken with Quinoa & Vegetable Medley
dinners.note: Free night. Chicken over quinoa with a colorful mix of zucchini and bell pepper — the kind of plate the "eat the rainbow" anti-inflammatory advice is pointing at.

ingredients.item: Olive oil — Jake scant 1¼ tbsp, Laine scant 1 tbsp
Ground turmeric — Jake ½ tsp, Laine ⅓ tsp
Lemon juice — Jake ½ tbsp, Laine scant ½ tbsp

steps: Cook the quinoa according to package directions.
Season the chicken with the spice mix and turmeric. Sear in olive oil 6–7 min per side until cooked through. Rest 5 min, slice.
In the same pan, sauté the zucchini, bell pepper, and garlic 4–5 min until just tender.
Plate quinoa and vegetables, top with sliced chicken, finish with a squeeze of lemon. Jake gets more of everything.

dinners.name: Mediterranean Cod & White Bean Skillet with Spinach
dinners.note: Second fish night. Light and simple — cod, cannellini beans, tomato, and spinach, nothing fried or heavy.

ingredients.item: Cannellini beans — Jake scant ½ can, Laine ⅓ can, rinsed
Diced tomatoes (canned) — Jake ⅔ cup, Laine scant ½ cup
Olive oil — Jake 1 tbsp, Laine scant ¾ tbsp
Lemon juice — Jake ½ tbsp, Laine scant ½ tbsp

steps: Pat the cod dry, season with spice mix. Sear in olive oil 3–4 min per side until just cooked through, remove.
In the same pan, add garlic, diced tomatoes, and cannellini beans, simmer 4–5 min.
Stir in the spinach until just wilted. Flake the cod back in gently, finish with lemon juice.
Jake gets more of everything.

dinners.name: Turmeric Chickpea & Vegetable Bowl
dinners.note: Vegetarian night, and a very classic anti-inflammatory combination — turmeric and chickpeas, roasted vegetables, a light lemony dressing, feta kept light-handed rather than loaded on.

ingredients.item: Garbanzo beans — Jake scant ½ can, Laine ⅓ can, rinsed
Sweet potato — Jake ~65g, Laine ~50g, roasted in small cubes
Olive oil — Jake scant 1 tbsp, Laine scant ¾ tbsp
Ground turmeric — Jake ¾ tsp, Laine ½ tsp
Lemon juice — Jake ½ tbsp, Laine scant ½ tbsp
Feta cheese, reduced fat — Jake ¾oz (24g), Laine ⅔oz (20g)
Greek yogurt (plain nonfat) — Jake ~1¾ tbsp, Laine ~1½ tbsp, stirred through

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Toss the sweet potato cubes with a little olive oil and roast 20 min. Steam the broccoli separately.
Cook the quinoa according to package directions.
Warm the garbanzo beans in a pan with garlic, turmeric, and spice mix, 3–4 min.
Combine quinoa, roasted sweet potato, broccoli, and garbanzo beans in a bowl. Dress with olive oil and lemon juice.
Top with crumbled feta and a dollop of Greek yogurt. Jake gets the bigger bowl.

dinners.name: Veggie & Avocado Egg White Scramble with Whole Grain Toast
dinners.note: Standing breakfast-for-dinner. Avocado stands in for a heavier cheese pour this time — still rich and satisfying, just from a different kind of fat. Feta stays light-handed rather than loaded.

ingredients.item: Liquid egg whites — Jake ¾ cup, Laine scant ½ cup
Avocado — Jake ½, Laine ⅓, sliced on top
Feta cheese, reduced fat — Jake ⅗oz (18g), Laine ½oz (15g)
Whole grain bread — Jake 2 slices, Laine 1 slice, toasted
Olive oil — Jake ½ tbsp, Laine ⅓ tbsp

steps: Sauté cherry tomatoes, bell pepper, and garlic in olive oil, 2–3 min.
Beat the eggs and egg whites together, pour in. Scramble gently over medium-low until just set.
Fold in the spinach at the end, season with spice mix. Crumble the feta through lightly.
Toast the bread. Serve the scramble topped with sliced avocado, toast alongside. Jake gets the bigger portion.

jakeLunch.name: Turmeric-Ginger Chicken & Quinoa Bowl
jakeLunch.note: Sunday-batch, 5 containers, no fish. Chicken simmered in a light turmeric-tomato sauce with spinach wilted in, over quinoa — same saucy, everything-in-one-container format as last week's pork bowl, so nothing needs adding after reheating.

ingredients.item: Chicken breast — ~3.6 lbs total (330g raw per container)
Diced tomatoes (canned) — scant ⅔ cup per container
Ground turmeric — scant ⅛ tsp per container
Olive oil — scant 1 tbsp per container
Lemon juice — scant 1 tbsp per container

steps: Cook all the quinoa at once.
Cube the chicken. Sear in batches in olive oil until browned on the outside.
Add garlic, turmeric, diced tomatoes, and lemon juice to the pan. Return the chicken, simmer 8–10 min until cooked through and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Stir in the spinach at the end, just until wilted.
Divide quinoa and the saucy chicken evenly across 5 containers.

laineLunch.name: Cold Tuna & Black Bean Mason Jar
laineLunch.note: Standing cold format, unchanged — already a pretty lean, anti-inflammatory-friendly lunch as it stands.
laineLunch.dressingNote: Olive oil + lemon juice, kept separate and added just before eating.

ingredients.item: Canned tuna in water — 1 can per jar (5 cans total)
Black beans — ~¼ can per jar, rinsed
Avocado — ½ avocado per jar, added fresh when eating
Olive oil — 1 tbsp per jar (dressing, separate)
Lemon juice — scant ½ tbsp per jar

steps: Drain tuna, rinse black beans. Dice cucumber and bell pepper.
Layer each jar: black beans → tuna → cucumber → bell pepper.
Portion the dressing into a small separate container per jar.
To eat: add dressing and fresh-cut avocado, stir, eat straight from the jar.

laineBreakfasts.name: Greek Yogurt Parfait
steps: Spoon yogurt into a bowl. Top with thawed berries and flaxseed.

laineBreakfasts.name: Spinach & Feta Egg White Scramble

ingredients.item: Pinch oregano, thyme, cumin, paprika, salt

steps: Sauté cherry tomatoes 1–2 min in a dry nonstick pan until they start to soften.
Add egg whites, scramble over medium-low until just set.
Toss in spinach at the end. Top with feta and a pinch of spice mix.

laineBreakfasts.name: Birch Benders Waffles + Berries
laineBreakfasts.note: Standing Sunday-morning waffles, separate from Sunday's breakfast-for-dinner — unchanged.

ingredients.item: Birch Benders pancake/waffle mix — ½ cup dry

steps: Mix batter: mix + egg whites + water per package. Stir in flaxseed.
Cook in a preheated waffle iron 3–4 min until crisp.
Top with thawed berries.

laineSnacks.name: Cucumber + Hummus
laineSnacks.desc: ¾ cucumber sliced + hummus for dipping.

laineSnacks.name: Greek Yogurt + Berries
laineSnacks.desc: 1 Oikos Triple Zero + small handful thawed berries.

jakeSnacks.name: Apple & Almond Butter
jakeSnacks.desc: 1 apple, sliced, with almond butter — swapped in for the usual cheddar pairing this week for a lighter, nuts-based fat instead.

jakeSnacks.name: Roasted Chickpeas + Almonds
jakeSnacks.desc: ¼ cup roasted chickpeas + a small handful of almonds.

jakeSnacks.name: Greek Yogurt + Almonds
jakeSnacks.desc: 1 container plain Greek yogurt + a small handful of almonds.

Must Buy: Frozen pork loin — have on hand (Monday roast + Tuesday leftovers). If it's less than ~1.15 lbs total, grab a bit more.
Chicken breast — ~4.7 lbs total (Thursday dinner + Jake's 5-container lunch batch)
Fresh ginger — 1 small knob (sauce + Wednesday salmon)
Zucchini, bell peppers — for Thursday's medley + Sunday + Laine's lunch/snacks
Baby spinach — larger bag (Friday, Jake's lunch, Sunday, breakfast scramble)
Canned tuna in water — 5 cans (Laine's lunch)
Check Supply: Ground turmeric, quinoa (dry) — both used often this week, worth double-checking you have enough of each
Garbanzo beans, cannellini beans, black beans, diced tomatoes (canned) — a couple cans each
Feta cheese, reduced fat — small amount needed (Saturday, Sunday, breakfast scramble) — kept light-handed this week
Greek yogurt (plain nonfat) — 1 tub (sauce batch + Saturday)
Almond butter — for the swapped-in Monday snack
Olive oil, garlic, lemon juice — used most nights
Frozen mixed berries, ground flaxseed — breakfast staples
Hummus, roasted chickpeas, almonds, cottage cheese — snack staples
Oregano / thyme / cumin / paprika — restock if low
Already Have: Cheddar cheese, shredded — not used this week; whatever's left from a couple weeks ago keeps fine
